facts.raw_span: abdominal pain that began around the umbilicus 2 days earlier and migrated to the right lower quadrant
no prior abdominal surgeries or systemic disease
denied anorexia, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, weight loss, night sweats, diarrhea, or constipation
afebrile
heart rate was 86 bpm
blood pressure was 130/95 mm Hg
voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant
minimal tenderness elsewhere
white-cell count of 15,600/mL
hemoglobin of 14.2 g/dL
plain abdominal X-rays demonstrated several air–fluid levels without free air under the diaphragm
ultrasound assessment was interpreted as compatible with plastron appendicitis

concepts.why: The patient's abdominal pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, voluntary guarding, elevated white-cell count, and imaging findings compatible with plastron appendicitis support this diagnosis.
The ultrasound assessment compatible with plastron appendicitis, along with the patient's clinical presentation and laboratory findings, supports this specific type of appendicitis.
The presence of abdominal pain and air-fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays could also suggest intussusception, although the ultrasound findings are more specific for appendicitis.
The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings could also be consistent with cecal diverticulitis, although the imaging findings are more suggestive of appendicitis.
The patient's abdominal pain and elevated white-cell count could also be due to Meckel's diverticulitis, although this diagnosis is less likely given the specific location and nature of the pain.
